03-072.r: Ayurveda ('Science of Life') → first appears in the Atharvaveda; Ayurveda is the Upaveda of the Atharvaveda.

03-073.r: Rigvedic religion → polytheistic. Gods of sky (Varuna, Mitra, Surya, Vishnu), space (Indra, Rudra), earth (Agni, Brihaspati, Soma).

03-074.r: Most Rigvedic hymns → Indra (about 250); next → Agni (about 200).
03-074.h: Indra 250, Agni 200: the war-god leads, fire follows.

03-075.r: Rigvedic war-god → Indra: storm-god and sky-god who wields the thunderbolt; most hymns are devoted to him.

03-077.r: Most Rigvedic hymns → Indra; second most → Agni.
03-077.t: If Indra is not among the options, choose Agni.

03-078.r: Indra → god of thunder, lightning and rain; king of Svarga; most popular early Vedic god and war-god. Guardian of moral order (Rita) → Varuna.
03-078.t: Guardian of Rita is Varuna, not Indra.

03-081.r: 800 B.C. to 600 B.C. → Brahmana era; Sutra period → about seventh or sixth century B.C. to third century B.C.

03-082.r: Gayatri Mantra → Rigveda; composed by Brahmarshi Vishwamitra; prays that God illuminate our intellect to the righteous path.

03-085.r: Mantra in the Upanayana of Kshatriyas → Trishtubh mantra (symbol of martial, heroic qualities).
03-085.t: Not Gayatri: for Kshatriya Upanayana the book's answer is Trishtubh.

03-086.r: Five marks of the Puranas → Sarga (creation), Pratisarga (re-creation), Vansa (sages, gods), Manvantara (Manu periods), Vanshanucharita (royal genealogy).

03-087.r: Number of Puranas → 18 (e.g., Matsya, Vishnu, Vayu, Bhagavat, Garuda, Skanda).

03-088.r: Upanishads do contain parables (two birds in Kathopanishad, Mundaka, Svetasvatara); Upanishads are older than Puranas → only statement 2 correct.

03-089.r: Vishnu Purana → Mauryan dynasty; Vayu Purana → Gupta dynasty; Matsya Purana → Andhra Satavahana dynasty. Both statements correct.

03-090.r: Shrimad Bhagavad Gita → originally in Sanskrit; 700 verses; part of the Mahabharata.

03-091.r: Mahabharata's original name → Jaya / Jayasamhita (8,800 shlokas); now 100,000 shlokas ('Shatasahasri Samhita'); attributed to Veda Vyasa.

03-093.r: Churning of the ocean: serpent Vasuki → churning rope; Mount Mandara → churning rod; Vishnu as Kurma supported the mountain.

03-094.r: Untouchability took clear shape in the Dharmashastra phase (early Christian era), when Brahmanical religion was rising.

03-095.r: 'Satyameva Jayate' ('truth alone triumphs') → Mundakopanishad; India's national motto at the base of the national emblem, adopted 26 January 1950.

03-098.r: 'Tamsoma Jyotirgamaya' (lead us from darkness to light) → Brihadaranyaka Upanishad.

03-099.r: Not Rigvedic → Gargi (later Vedic/Upanishadic philosopher). Ghosha, Apala, Vishvavara → Rigvedic women seers.

03-101.r: Upanishad meaning 'white horse' → Shvetashvatara (in Yajurveda); not among the options → 'none of these'.

03-102.r: Satyakama Jabala legend (challenges stigma of an unmarried mother) → Chhandogya Upanishad (chapter IV).

03-103.r: Basic script of Rigveda (book) → Brahmi. Rigveda: 10 Mandalas, 1028 Suktas, 10552 Mantras; 21 branches (Patanjali); its priest → Hota.

03-105.r: Avesta (Zoroastrian scripture similar to the Rigveda) → Iran.

03-106.r: 'Aghanya' (not to be killed) in the Rigveda → cow.

03-109.r: Correct: Rigvedic Aryans used coat of mail and helmet; Indus people left no such evidence. Wrong: Indus knew only copper and bronze, not iron; horse statement wrong → 1 only.

03-110.r: Most valuable property in early Rigvedic period → cow (cattle breeding main activity; cow a medium of exchange).

03-111.r: Indus Valley Civilization → urban; Rigvedic society → pastoral; Later Vedic society → agrarian; Medieval period → landlordism.
03-111.h: Time order Indus, Rigvedic, Later Vedic, Medieval = Urban, Pastoral, Agrarian, Landlordism.

03-112.r: Odd one out → Kosa (treasury); Kula, Vansha, Gotra relate to family and lineage.

03-113.r: Total Sanskaras → 16: three before birth, twelve during life, one after death; Upanayana most important.

03-114.r: Teacher who taught a portion of Veda/Vedangas for livelihood → Upadhyaya.

04-001.r: Gautama Buddha (Siddhartha) → born 563 B.C., Lumbini near Kapilavastu (Nepal); father Shuddhodana (Shakya chief), mother Mayadevi (Koliya clan); left home at 29 (Mahabhinishkramana).

04-005.r: Another name of Buddha: none given. Parth and Gudakesh → names of Arjuna; Mihir, Prachhanna → not Buddha → 'none of these' (CGPSC key chose Prachhanna).

04-006.r: Lumbini as Buddha's birthplace → Mauryan Ashoka's Rummindei pillar inscription; Ashoka visited after his 20th regnal year, exempted bali, fixed an eighth share.

04-009.r: Buddha's Mahaparinirvana → Kushinagar (Kusinara) in the Malla republic; earlier he ate at Chund's mango grove in Pava, the Malla capital.

04-013.r: Mahaparinirvana temple → Kushinagar (U.P.); reclining dying Buddha of Chunar sandstone, unearthed in 1876-77.

04-014.r: Kingdoms linked with Buddha's life → Kosala and Magadha (not Avanti or Gandhara).

04-015.r: Last person converted by Buddha → Subhadda, at Kushinagar; Buddha fell ill at Pava after eating Sukaramaddava offered by Chund.

04-017.r: Buddha's last rainy season → Vaishali (Beluva suburb), at about eighty, with disciple Ananda.

04-018.r: Nirvana in Buddhism → extinction of the flame of desire (literally 'blown out'); desire is the cause of pain.

04-019.r: Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (Bihar) → Gautama Buddha.

04-020.r: Alara Kalama → teacher of the Buddha (taught him meditation).

04-021.r: First sermon (Dhammachakkapavattana) → Sarnath. Four holy places: Lumbini (birth), Bodhgaya (enlightenment), Sarnath (first sermon), Kushinagar (death).
hi: Turning the Wheel of Dharma (धर्मचक्र प्रवर्तन)

04-027.r: Most sermons of Buddha → Shravasti, capital of Kosala (most of his disciples came from Kosala).

04-028.r: Buddha visited Kaushambi in the reign of Udayana; Udayana, influenced by Pindola Bharadwaj, gave Ghoshitaram Vihar to the Sangha.

04-029.r: First Buddhist Council → Rajgriha (Saptaparni Cave); patron Ajatashatru; president Mahakassapa; Ananda recited Sutta, Upali recited Vinaya.

04-034.r: First Buddhist Council → Saptaparni Cave, Rajgriha (Rajgir), under Magadh king Ajatashatru, just after Buddha's death.

04-035.r: Fourth Buddhist Council → Kundalavana, Kashmir, under Kanishka; president Vasumitra, deputy Ashvaghosha; Buddhism split into Mahayana and Hinayana.

04-041.r: Mahayana features → deification of Buddha, path of Bodhisattvas (delay own salvation to help all beings), image worship and rituals → all three.

04-042.r: Buddhist Councils in order → Rajgriha (Ajatashatru) → Vaishali (Kalasoka, Sabakami; 100 years after Buddha) → Pataliputra (Ashoka) → Kundalavana (Kanishka).

04-043.r: Buddhist Councils order → Rajagriha → Vaishali → Pataliputra → Kundalvana (2, 1, 4, 3); first under Ajatashatru, third at Pataliputra.

04-050.r: Council presidents: First → Mahakashyapa; Second → Sabakami; Third → Moggaliputta Tissa; Fourth → Vasumitra.

04-051.r: Buddha: birth → Lumbini; enlightenment → Bodhgaya; first sermon → Sarnath (Rishipattan); death → Kushinagar.

04-052.r: Wheel with deer in Indian art → Buddha's first preaching at Mrigadava (Sarnath).
04-052.h: Mrigadava = deer park, so deer + wheel = first sermon.

04-053.r: Buddha symbols: birth → lotus; first sermon → Dharma Chakra; enlightenment → Bodhi tree; great departure → horse.

04-054.r: Karmapa Lama → Kangyupa sect of Tibetan Buddhism.
